correctness.rationale: For an orthogonal projection \(\mathcal E\), the decompositions \(\rho=\mathcal E\rho+R\) and \(\sigma=\mathcal E\sigma+S\) are Hilbert--Schmidt orthogonal. Substitution into superfidelity turns the entire difference into \(\lVert(a,R)\rVert\lVert(b,S)\rVert-\langle(a,R),(b,S)\rangle\), which is nonnegative by one Cauchy--Schwarz inequality. Projective pinching is self-adjoint and idempotent in the Hilbert--Schmidt inner product, trace preserving and state preserving. No numerical or finite-dimensional spot check substitutes for the proof.

value.rationale: The result answers an explicit published question about a computationally and experimentally motivated fidelity surrogate. It identifies a maximal natural positive mechanism absent for arbitrary channels: orthogonal coarse-graining. The exact deficit and equality characterization explain why pinching works and extend the result beyond the originally posed projective-measurement class, rather than merely checking isolated examples.
